questions.title: — The Inclined Ladder Against a Smooth Wall
questions.question: A uniform ladder rests against a smooth vertical wall and a rough horizontal floor. Its weight is 200 N, acting at its midpoint. The horizontal reaction at the wall is 60 N. The ladder makes an angle of 45^° with the floor. Find the vertical reaction of the floor, assuming the ladder is in equilibrium.

questions.explanation:
The wall is smooth, so its reaction is horizontal. It has no vertical component. Therefore, the floor must balance the entire weight vertically:


R_V-W=0



R_V=200 N


The horizontal reaction determines the frictional force at the floor, not the vertical reaction.

Initially,


M₁=50(0.8)sin60^°
=20sqrt3≈34.64 N m

questions.title: — The Child on a Seesaw Moves
questions.question: A 30 kg child sits 2 m from the fulcrum on one side of a seesaw. A 20 kg child sits 3 m from the fulcrum on the opposite side. The seesaw is initially horizontal. The 30 kg child moves 0.5 m farther away. What happens to the net moment? Take g=10 m s^.

options.text: It becomes 150 N m towards the 30 kg child.
It becomes 150 N m towards the 20 kg child.

It becomes 300 N m towards the 30 kg child.

questions.explanation:
Initially, the moments balance:


300(2)=200(3)=600 N m


After moving, the first child is 2.5 m away:


M₁=300(2.5)=750 N m


The opposing moment remains 600 N m.


M_{net}=750-600=150 N m


**Concept tested:** The effect of changing only one person's distance from a pivot.

To arrange elements according to their physical states alone
To organize elements systematically and reveal relationships among their properties

options.text: S is more acidic than P because its pH is closer to 7.
Q contains no hydrogen ions because it is neutral.
R is alkaline, while P is more acidic than S.
P and R are both acidic because neither has pH 7.

questions.explanation:
At room temperature, pH below 7 indicates an acidic solution, pH 7 indicates neutrality, and pH above 7 indicates an alkaline solution. Therefore, P (pH 2) is more acidic than S (pH 5), while R (pH 11) is alkaline. Neutral water still contains hydrogen ions, represented in aqueous solution as hydronium ions, H_3O⁺, and hydroxide ions, OH⁻, in equal concentrations. Neutral does not mean ion-free.

Tube C must contain sodium hydroxide, NaOH, and Tube B must contain pure water, H_2O.

questions.explanation:
Universal indicator generally shows red in strongly acidic solutions, yellow in acidic solutions, green near pH 7, and blue in alkaline solutions. The colours indicate approximate pH, not the chemical identity or concentration of a solution. Thus, red alone cannot prove that an acid is strong, and green does not prove that a sample is pure water.

questions.question: Which sequence gives the correct order of size for the species O^, O, and O^?

options.text: O⁺ > O > O²⁻
O > O²⁻ > O⁺
O²⁻ > O > O⁺
O > O⁺ > O²⁻

questions.explanation:
Gaining electrons to form O²⁻ increases electron–electron repulsion and expands the electron cloud. Losing an electron to form O⁺ generally contracts it. Thus, O²⁻ is largest and O⁺ is smallest.

**Tempting distractor:** Option A reverses the effect of electron gain and loss on size.

questions.title: Board-style Distinguishing electron affinity and electronegativity
questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Both properties have exactly the same definition
Electron affinity concerns the energy change when a gaseous atom gains an electron, while electronegativity describes attraction for shared bonding electrons
Electronegativity is the energy needed to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom
Electron affinity is determined only by the number of neutrons

questions.explanation:
Electron affinity relates to the energy change accompanying electron gain by an isolated gaseous atom. Electronegativity concerns the relative attraction for shared electrons in a chemical bond.

**Tempting distractor:** Option C defines ionisation energy, not electronegativity.

questions.title: Board-style Explaining the modern periodic law
questions.question: Why is atomic number a more reliable basis for periodic classification than atomic mass?

options.text: Atomic number changes when an atom forms an ion
Atomic mass is identical for all isotopes
Atomic number determines only the physical state of an element
Atomic number identifies nuclear charge and, in a neutral atom, the electron count that determines its electronic configuration

questions.explanation:
Atomic number equals the number of protons. In a neutral atom, it also equals the number of electrons. This determines the electronic configuration and explains the periodic recurrence of chemical properties. Atomic mass does not always give the correct order for elements with anomalous mass relationships.

**Tempting distractor:** Option B is false because isotopes of the same element have different mass numbers.

questions.question: A neutral representative element has four occupied shells and two valence electrons. Which option identifies its period and group correctly?

options.text: Period 2, Group 2
Period 4, Group 2
Period 4, Group 14
Period 2, Group 14

questions.explanation:

Option C incorrectly adds 10 to the valence-electron count even though this element belongs to the s-block.

questions.title: Comparing isoelectronic ions
questions.question: Consider O^, F⁻, Na⁺, and Mg^. Each has 10 electrons. Which order correctly arranges them from largest to smallest?

options.text: Mg²⁺>Na⁺>F⁻>O²⁻
F⁻>O²⁻>Na⁺>Mg²⁺
O²⁻>F⁻>Na⁺>Mg²⁺
Na⁺>Mg²⁺>O²⁻>F⁻

questions.explanation:
All four ions have 10 electrons. Their nuclear charges increase in the order O (8), F (9), Na (11), Mg (12). Greater nuclear charge pulls the same number of electrons more strongly inward, giving the stated size order.

Option A reverses the effect of nuclear charge on the size of an isoelectronic series.

questions.title: Finding the next element in the same group
questions.question: Potassium has atomic number 19. Calcium has atomic number 20. The next element after calcium in Period 4 is scandium, atomic number 21. Which element is the next member of Group 1 after potassium, and what is its atomic number?

options.text: Calcium, 20
Scandium, 21
Rubidium, 37
Sodium, 11

questions.explanation:
Group 1 contains Li (3), Na (11), K (19), and Rb (37). The next Group 1 element after potassium is rubidium, atomic number 37. One must not simply add one to potassium's atomic number because calcium through krypton occupy the intervening positions.
